subject: Want to do something like aaply, but group by factors

messages.author: d67e993806d464c5
messages.subject: Want to do something like aaply, but group by factors
parts:
Hi! I'm a new, yet enthusiastic, user of the reshape and plyr
packages (thanks, Hadley!). I have this problem that I am able to do
easily, but slowly, with melt and cast, and would like to see if it
would be more efficient to use plyr.

I have a 3-dimensional array of values N people x T months x K
parameters. I also have a factor for each of the people, with L
levels in the factor. What I want to do is get the mean, across
people within each level of the factor, for each of the T*K month-
parameters combinations. So my input X is an N x T x K array, and the
output Y should be an L x T x K array.

The first thing I did was name each of the rows of X by the level name
(yes, this means rows will have the same names--not good). Then,
Using the reshape functions, I can get what I want:

dimnames(X) <- list(Level=level.names, Month=1:T, Parameter=1:K)
X.melt <- melt(X)
Y <- cast(X.melt, Level ~ Month ~ Parameter, fun.aggregate=mean,
value="value")

This gets me what I want, but I'm hoping that plyr might work faster.

One thing I considered was

Y <- aaply(X, c(2,3), mean)

which gives me the Month-Parameter means across all people, but
doesn't split by factor.

I also tried

Y <- aaply(X, c(2,3), mean, subset=as.factor(level.names))

with no difference in the output.

I suppose one way would be to melt X into a dataframe before using
daply, but then I still have to do the resource-intensive melt step.
But what I'm really looking for is a way to use a plyr function that
operates on an arbitrary "chunk" of data, where the cut points are
determined by factors. Is this possible?

Thanks in advance for the help and advice,

Michael Braun
MIT Sloan School of Management
bra...@mit.edu

messages.author: a60b2109152be9df
messages.subject: Re: Want to do something like aaply, but group by factors
parts:
I haven't checked this throughly, but does this do what you want?

## number of levels
L <- 10
## number of individual observations (4 each level)
N <- L*4
## number of periods
T <- 2
## number of features
K <- 3
## array
a <- array(rnorm(N*T*K), dim=c(N,T,K))
## the levels
l <- rep(1:L, 4)
## *aply it
res <- laply(1:L, function(x) aaply(a[l==x,,],c(2,3),mean))

messages.subject: Re: Want to do something like aaply, but group by factors
parts:
Yes, that worked perfectly. Thank you.

I am curious about why you suggest using laply instead of aaply, since
1:L is an array. Is it just to save that extra parameter in the
function call?

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Want to do something like aaply, but group by factors
parts:
> I am curious about why you suggest using laply instead of aaply, since
> 1:L is an array.  Is it just to save that extra parameter in the
> function call?

A couple of points:

* In R lingo, 1:L is a vector, not an array

> is.array(1:10)
[1] FALSE

* laply isn't named very well - it really should be vaply, where v = vector.


However, that solution is still a bit of a hack. I think the ideal
solution would be a way to flexibly create iterators that can
partition up any data structure the way you want, instead of just the
three fixed iterators plyr currently provides. It seems unlikely I'll
have the time to do this in the near future, however :(

Hadley
